item.title: Trump Struggles to Sell Voters on the Economy
item.description:
Nov 1st, 2026
Trump Struggles to Sell Voters on the Economy
Bloomberg News Senior Executive Editor Wes Kosova tells Bloomberg This Weekend that President Donald Trump is struggling to convince voters the economy is strong as higher fuel prices and affordability concerns weigh on his support, including among Republicans. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, Kosova says Trump’s last-minute promises of financial relief may have limited power to change voters’ perceptions, while the prolonged Iran war adds uncertainty over when energy prices could ease.

By Stephen StapczynskiNovember 1, 2026 at 9:23 AM UTCUpdated on November 1, 2026 at 2:48 PM UTCBookmark

Pakistan negotiated with Iran to secure safe passage for liquefied natural gas carrier Al Mayeda before the ship was attacked near the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, according to people with direct knowledge of the matter.
The Marshall Islands-flagged vessel was sailing toward the waterway loaded with LNG from Qatar when it came under fire, the people said, asking not to be named as they are not authorized to speak to the media. Just hours earlier, Iranian authorities were understood to have provided a green light, they added.

Russian President Vladimir Putin has agreed to halt the recruitment of Ghanaians to fight in Ukraine after President John Mahama raised concerns about the practice, according to Ghana’s foreign minister.
Putin said Ghanaians will no longer be allowed to participate in the war, whether through irregular recruitment or as volunteers, Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa said in a Facebook post following last week’s Russia-Africa summit.

item.title: AI Talent War Spreads to Wall Street
item.description:

AI Talent War Spreads to Wall Street
Bloomberg Senior Markets Reporter Justina Lee tells Bloomberg This Weekend that quantitative trading firms are competing with AI labs for top scientists and researchers, with first-year compensation for some PhDs reaching as much as $800,000. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, Lee explains how firms are using fellowships, university sponsorships and recruiting events to compete with AI companies offering lucrative pay, equity and the chance to work on cutting-edge technology.

Morgan Stanley’s Mike Wilson says he sees a few “clearing events” ahead for the stock market that have the potential to take it lower temporarily, creating a great opportunity for investors to pile back in.
The bank’s head US equity strategist pointed to a number of things that could bring the S&P 500 Index down about 9% from its last record to 7,100 — primarily the midterm elections, stress over artificial intelligence spending and liquidity constraints.

Tech Selloff Could Ease Pressure on the Fed
BMO Capital Markets Senior Economist and Managing Director Jennifer Lee tells Bloomberg This Weekend that heavy AI investment has helped drive interest rates and inflation pressures higher, while a cooling in the sector could make the Federal Reserve’s job easier. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, Lee says the US economy remains robust but points to softer consumer spending and wage growth as investors await fresh labor data and another round of technology earnings.

Brazil’s market selloff has delivered a stark warning to emerging-market investors: crowded trades can unravel with alarming speed.
Popular bets ranging from Asian artificial intelligence-linked stocks to Hungarian bonds and the South African rand are facing fresh scrutiny after an election shock sent Brazilian shares and the real tumbling, exposing how one-sided positioning can amplify market reversals.

Brooks Steps Up Global Push as Running Boom Builds
Brooks Running CEO Dan Sheridan tells Bloomberg This Weekend that a global running boom and consumers’ continued focus on health and wellness are helping drive growth, with the company expanding in markets including Europe and China. Speaking with host Lisa Mateo, Sheridan says Brooks is also expanding its lifestyle business and physical stores while navigating tariffs and supply-chain disruptions without passing all of those costs on to consumers.

item.title: IMO Chief Says Strait of Hormuz Remains Unsafe
item.description:
Bloomberg This Weekend • Nov 1st, 2026
IMO Chief Says Strait of Hormuz Remains Unsafe
International Maritime Organization Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the Strait of Hormuz remains unsafe for commercial shipping, with vessel traffic sharply below pre-conflict levels as attacks, mines and other hazards threaten ships and seafarers. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, Dominguez says the disruption is raising global fuel and shipping costs while forcing the industry to develop alternative routes and strengthen supply-chain resilience.

item.title: The $40 Trillion Problem Washington Won’t Talk About
item.description: America’s national debt has climbed past $40 trillion and persistent deficits are putting upward pressure on long-term interest rates. Economists including Natasha Sarin of the Yale Budget Lab argue that heavier government borrowing ultimately filters through to households in the form of higher mortgages, car loans and other financing costs. Former House Speaker Paul Ryan says the country can still change course, but doing so will require confronting politically difficult questions around entitlement spending, taxes and the future of Social Security before markets force Washington to act. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: OPEC+ Leaves Oil Output Targets Unchanged for December
item.description: Seven members of the OPEC+ group of oil producers agreed to keep output quotas unchanged in December, after unwinding the last of their voluntary cuts in September.

item.title: Australia’s Home Prices Fall Further Ahead of Expected Rate Hike
item.description: Australia’s home prices tumbled for a seventh straight month and are on track for the biggest fall in 40 years, a private gauge showed, as the Reserve Bank is expected to increase borrowing costs again this week.

item.title: OPEC+ Sticks With Plan for Steady Oil Output Quotas in December
item.description: Major OPEC+ nations reaffirmed plans to keep oil production quotas unchanged in December as conflict in the Middle East continues to curb swaths of the group’s output.

item.title: Germany Misses Gas Storage Target as Cold Snap Sets In
item.description: Germany is set to miss its official target for filling natural gas storage sites, leaving it with a reduced buffer against surging winter demand.
